messages.author: 010fa11e67a0d0b7
messages.subject: Underdispersed occupancy model
parts:
Dear Unmark'ers,

I am evaluating the goodness of fit of a global model, prior to any model selection, and after a thorough selection of variables via spearman correlation and variance inflation factor (VIF), and
the addition of an autocovariate to correct for spatial autocorrelation of residuals.

I used the 'mb.gof.test' function of AICcmodavg package to test model fit, and although I got a good model fit, my data seems to be very underdispersed. So, my first question is, if the model
has a good fit, is underdispersion a problem at all?

Assuming it is, and as one possible cause might be poor model structure, I run all possible submodels removing just one variable. However, I keep getting good fit combined with high underdispersion.

Also, I read about possible next steps, which include set c-hat= 1 in model selection, or applying QAICc as information criteria, or both.

My second question is then, which of these possible next steps is the most appropriate?

Many thanks in advance for any thoughts shared.

Cheers,
Ana

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#Global model:

ms_all<-occu(~day+Patch_hq_VSI~Area+Perimeter+Shape_index+Isolation+Near_Crop+Near_Urban+Patch_hq_VSI+wood+shrub+grass+grst+soil+
crop_100+autocov_10,ms_occ)

#GOF

Pearson chi-square table:

Cohort Observed Expected Chi-square
00 0 18 18.02 0.00
01 0 3 3.71 0.14
10 0 4 2.86 0.46
11 0 17 17.41 0.01

Chi-square statistic = 0.6007
Number of bootstrap samples = 1000
P-value = 0.718

Quantiles of bootstrapped statistics:
0% 25% 50% 75% 100%
0.0052 0.5039 1.2314 2.4347 10.5798


Estimate of c-hat = 0.35

messages.author: 67eefb0e32c64fae
messages.subject: Re: Underdispersed occupancy model
parts:
Hi Ana,

You're right, that is a low c-hat value, but your p-value is not significant. So it is under-dispersed, but not significantly so.

I'm not an expert in this, but if this were my data, I would take a second look at the model structure, just to see if there's anything you can improve, but after that move on.

Best,

Sean
